children.text: Consider sketching a reaction diagram that depicts various components of a chemical reaction as described by the provided information, and remember how reactions are defined as exothermic or endothermic based on the potential energy of the bonds within the reactants and potential energy of the bonds within the products. For the reaction diagram, focus on which direction of the reaction, forward or reverse, has the higher activation energy to reach the transition state. The forward direction starts on the left with the potential energy level of the reactant molecules and moves to the right (forward direction) to reach the transition state when the reactant molecules collide with the minimum kinetic energy (activation energy) and proper orientation. The reverse direction starts on the right with the potential energy level of the product molecules and moves to the left (reverse direction) to reach the transition state when the product molecules collide with the minimum kinetic energy (activation energy) and proper orientation.

Correct. For the activation barrier of the reaction to be higher for the forward reaction compared to the reverse reaction, the potential energy level of the reactant molecules must be lower than the potential energy of the product molecules. By definition, an endothermic reaction means the potential energy of the bonds within the reactants is lower than the potential energy of the bonds within the products.

Since the reaction is exothermic, the reactant energy is lower than the product energy and thus the energy difference from reactant to transition state is greater than that from product to transition state.
